rubrics.justification: Correctly identifies an expanded Day-5 blastocyst with thinned zona and fair overall quality, but misstates the grading details by calling the ICM only moderate and implying B-grade TE when the provided Gardner score is 3AB (A-grade ICM, B-grade TE). Some image-based comments are reasonable but not especially precise.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, and first-cycle status well, and links these factors to prognosis. Minor overemphasis on morphology relative to other determinants keeps it from a top score.

The response is logically structured and generally consistent, with conclusions flowing from embryo morphology and patient factors. There is a mild inconsistency between the supplied 3AB grade and the narrative downgrading of ICM quality, and the implantation estimate may be somewhat broad.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice: transfer is reasonable, SET is appropriate at age 32, avoid unsupported add-ons, and lifestyle optimization is sensible. Small deviations include some imprecise commentary on endometrial thickness and morphology interpretation.

Provides practical next steps for the current transfer and contingency planning for future cycles, including SET, luteal support adherence, lifestyle changes, and when to consider further workup. Useful and specific, though not highly individualized beyond standard recommendations.
